transcript.text: My Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is sparking inside when I heat soup, little blue flashes on the right-hand wall and a crackling noise. I stopped it. Is it safe?

No—do not use it again until the cause is identified. Blue flashes and crackling inside a microwave are arcing, which can damage the oven and can potentially start a fire.

1. Unplug it and let it cool.
2. Check the soup container and anything else that was inside: no metal rim, foil lid, twist tie, metallic decoration, or spoon.
3. With it unplugged, inspect the cavity for food splashes, burnt marks, chipped paint/enamel, or a damaged/burnt-looking panel/cover on the right-hand wall (often the waveguide cover).
4. You can clean ordinary food residue from the cavity with a soft damp cloth and mild detergent, then dry it fully. Do not scrape, puncture, remove, or attempt to repair the wall cover or casing.
5. If there are scorch marks, damaged coating, a burned/warped cover, or it sparked despite using a microwave-safe container, do not test it again—arrange service through Panasonic/an authorised microwave repairer, or replace it.

Do not open the outer case: microwaves contain components that can retain a dangerous electrical charge even when unplugged.

If there was smoke, a persistent burning smell, or flames, keep it unplugged and do not use it at all.

It's unplugged now. No metal in it, just a plain plastic bowl with soup. There's a cardboard-like panel on the right wall with a black burnt spot and greasy splatter on it, and I did see a wisp of smoke from that spot once before it stopped when I turned it off. Should I replace that panel?

That sounds like the waveguide cover (usually a thin mica sheet), not ordinary cardboard. Grease and food deposits on it can carbonise and cause the blue arcing, crackling and smoke you saw.

Do not use the microwave again in its current state. The cover should be replaced, but use only the correct microwave-rated replacement for the Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ—never cardboard, tape, foil, or a random plastic sheet.

Because it has actually smoked and has a burnt spot:

• Arrange replacement through Panasonic/an authorised microwave repairer, or obtain the exact specified waveguide cover and have it fitted by a competent appliance technician.
• The area behind/around the cover and the cavity paint may also need inspection. If the metal cavity wall is scorched, pitted, or its coating has burned/chipped, it needs professional assessment; replacing the cover alone may not be enough.
• Do not operate it with the cover removed, even briefly.
• Do not remove the microwave’s outer casing.

If the only issue turns out to be a grease-stained but otherwise intact cover, cleaning may sometimes prevent arcing—but a black burn mark plus smoke means replacement/inspection is the sensible safe option.
